Nvidia: Scaling Quarterly Revenue Rapidly

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) primarily generates revenue by designing and selling advanced graphics processing units (GPUs), networking interconnect solutions, and accelerated computational platforms for data centers, personal computer gaming systems, enterprise professional visualization workstations, autonomous automotive applications, and cloud gaming subscription services.

It recently agreed to supply Amazon-owned AWS with additional graphics processing units and expanded its software partnership with Meta Platforms, while simultaneously introducing new hardware reference architectures intended to reduce initial infrastructure deployment time for its commercial enterprise customers.

SK Hynix: Expanding Memory Semiconductor Revenue

SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) primarily generates revenue by designing, manufacturing, and selling a wide variety of advanced memory semiconductors, including dynamic random-access memory and diverse flash memory products with specialized configurations tailored to meet application-specific customer needs across global technology markets.

It recently showcased its new tenth-generation flash memory technology and officially commenced shipments of its latest high-bandwidth memory products to customers, while separately navigating a suspended initial public offering for its United States memory subsidiary, Solidigm, and defending against an ongoing antitrust class action lawsuit.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue helps investors evaluate the total volume of products and services a company sells before deducting its operating costs, taxes, and other financial expenses. This metric reveals whether an organization is successfully attracting customers and growing its overall business volume over time.

Delivered total revenues in Q3 2026 of approximately $3.66 billion, exceeding guidance of $3.3 billion while growing 58.5%, the highest year-over-year revenue growth since our IPO.

In partnership with AMD, Arm, Broadcom, d-Matrix, Meta, Microsoft, and Qualcomm, Arista launched open standards-based rack-scale architectures for scale-up and scale-out AI networks.

In September 2026, Arista was added to the S&P 100, an index comprised of 100 major blue-chip companies across multiple industry groups.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., November 03, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE: ANET), an industry leader in data-driven, client-to-cloud networking for large AI, data center, campus, and routing environments, today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

"Arista registered another momentous quarter with the highest year-over-year revenue growth since our IPO and record profitability, surpassing even my high expectations," stated Jayshree Ullal, Chairperson and CEO of Arista Networks. "This strong momentum across customer sectors highlights our increased relevance for the generative and agentic AI era."

Third Quarter Financial Highlights

Revenue of $3.66 billion, an increase of 20.5% compared to the second quarter of 2026, and an increase of 58.5% from the third quarter of 2025.

GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 44.9% and 49.1%, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 42.4% and 48.6% in the third quarter of 2025.

GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.22 and $1.20, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.67 and $0.77 in the third quarter of 2025.

A reconciliation of the company's non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures has been provided in the financial statement tables included in this press release.

Commenting on the company's financial performance, Chantelle Breithaupt, CFO, said, "This quarter brought a true trifecta for our company, setting new record highs in revenue growth, net income, and EPS. I'm incredibly proud of the Arista team for their hard work in driving such outstanding performance for our shareholders."

Company Highlights

Arista announced open Ethernet rack-scale architectures for scale-up and scale-out AI fabrics – The new liquid-cooled portfolio leverages Ethernet for Scale-Up Networks (ESUN) and introduces the Etherlink™ SU-144 architecture, supporting up to 144 accelerators per rack in a single hop and scaling up to 1,024 XPUs via cross-rack topologies.

Arista detailed its scale-across networking strategy for distributed AI fabrics – Highlighting the flagship Arista 7800 AI Spine and unified Arista EOS®, the company outlined how Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) multiplane forwarding, deterministic routing, and real-time congestion signaling enable lossless, high-radix AI fabrics across geographically distributed data centers up to one million XPUs.

Arista expanded AI-driven software security across its development lifecycle – Collaborating with the likes of Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, Arista embedded domain-specific AI harnesses that accelerate proactive vulnerability discovery, building on the company's track record of low CVEs and no-downtime upgrades.

title: Aptos joins Solana and Ethereum in Bullish’s tokenized stock plan
detail:
Aptos joins Solana and Ethereum in Bullish’s tokenized stock plan
Neo
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 3:57 PM EST 3 min read
BLSH
SOL-USD
ETH-USD
META
Trade Bullish on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Wall Street's back office still runs on systems built decades ago. A stock trade can take a business day to settle, and markets close every evening and weekend.

Bullish, the New York Stock Exchange-listed digital asset company, wants to change that by putting company shares on public blockchains, and Aptos is now part of that plan.

On Nov. 3, Bullish named Aptos, Solana and Ethereum as the first networks for its equity tokenization services.

Tokenization means turning an asset, in this case a company's shares, into digital tokens that live on a blockchain.

Aptos is a layer-1 blockchain, a base network that apps are built on, originally incubated at Meta.

Bullish already works with Solana. The company says it plans to expand to Aptos and Ethereum, giving companies that issue shares a choice of where their tokenized stock lives.

It hasn't given a launch date for either network.

Related: Binance says its $6.3 billion hack started with a fake job offer

Big money managers are already on Aptos

Aptos says its transactions are finalized in under a second for a fraction of a cent, and that tokenized funds from asset managers including Franklin Templeton and Apollo already run on it.

Those funds are real-world assets: traditional financial products, such as money market funds or credit, issued as tokens on a blockchain.

Aptos argues that hosting them shows large institutions already trust its network with regulated products.

The fee claim holds up in outside research. A Blockworks Research report published Oct. 20 put the median Aptos transaction fee at about $0.0003, even after the network raised fees tenfold in March.

The same report counted about $1.6 billion in stablecoins on Aptos. Stablecoins are tokens pegged to the U.S. dollar, and they're the cash that tokenized assets usually trade against.

Aptos has also added privacy features that matter to institutions. Confidential APT went live on mainnet in September, letting users hide balances and transfer amounts if they choose.

TheStreet Roundtable's Coverage of Aptos:

Aptos exec: Wall Street still needs treasury stocks

Aptos Labs and five blockchain groups ask SEC for clearer crypto rules

Aptos cuts APT supply growth by 70% after token overhaul, report finds

In October, Aptos launched an encrypted mempool, a protected waiting area for pending transactions that stops others from seeing trades before they go through and jumping ahead of them.

Aptos is also preparing for the long term. In April, Coinbase's Quantum Advisory Board named Aptos one of the two layer-1 networks most ready for future quantum computers, which could one day break today's encryption.

We just published the list of the 10 Best Tech Stocks for the Next 5 Years and Meta Platforms (META) ranked 6th on this list.

Big Tech just had a week investors will remember. At its low on Friday, Alphabet had lost $477 billion in market value for the week, its worst week ever and the second-biggest weekly wipeout for any US-listed stock by Yahoo Finance's calculations, Yahoo Finance reported on October 30.

Most of the damage came Thursday, when the Google parent lost $475 billion in a single session after its third-quarter results. For October as a whole, Yahoo Finance calculated a loss of about $766 billion at Friday's low. That is the second-biggest monthly loss ever for a US-listed company, behind only SpaceX's roughly $822 billion drop in July.

5 Best "Moonshot" Tech Stocks to Buy According to Short Sellers

Photo by Arturo Añez on Unsplash

Heavy Losses Spread Beyond Alphabet

Alphabet wasn't alone. SpaceX, Intel and Nvidia each lost more than $100 billion in market value this week, according to Yahoo Finance. Intel fell as much as 30% on Friday after a weak outlook, its steepest drop in decades, and Amazon shed about $70 billion after reporting results Thursday. Software stocks took some of the sharpest hits in percentage terms, with ServiceNow and Fortinet down roughly 25% to 33%.

Nvidia was among the biggest losers. Our analysis of whether Nvidia can sustain its exceptional margins as it becomes more than a chipmaker looks at what keeps its profits so high.

UBS Argues Against Heading for the Exits

Not all the money left the market. Eli Lilly, Tesla and SK Hynix added about $370 billion in combined value over the same stretch, even as the Magnificent Seven stumbled, Yahoo Finance said.

UBS's chief investment office argued against retreating. Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, the bank's CIO Americas and global head of equities, wrote on Friday that further volatility does not make leaving markets an effective way to protect a portfolio from drawdowns. She said UBS still sees scope for equity gains overall and believes investors should focus on "building a resilient portfolio that includes exposure beyond tech."

The selloff also left Alphabet's price-to-earnings ratio at its lowest in more than a decade, Yahoo Finance noted. You might also be interested in reading our piece on why Alphabet's low P/E is misleading even as the AI opportunity looks real.

Meta runs Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp, and it sells advertising across all four. Investors like how well it uses AI to make those ads more effective.

Third-quarter revenue was $64.60 billion, up 26% from a year earlier, and advertising brought in $63,061 million of it. The number of ads Meta delivered rose 10%, and the average price per ad rose 14%, so the company grew on both measures at once. That mix shows growth did not rely on higher prices alone, which helps explain why advertisers keep spending. Meta said its family of apps reached 3.64 billion daily active people on average in September, up 3% from a year earlier.

title: Snap Settled a Social Media Addiction Suit. Here’s What Its November 4 Report Has to Prove
detail:
Snap Settled a Social Media Addiction Suit. Here’s What Its November 4 Report Has to Prove
Nikko Henson

META
Trade META on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Snap Settled a Social Media Addiction Suit. Here's What Its November 4 Report Has to Prove ©Marcela Ruth Romero from Ruty Romero's Images and mohamed abdelghaffar from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Snap (SNAP) settled a social media addiction lawsuit on November 2, two days before opening arguments were scheduled to begin in Los Angeles.

Meta Platforms (META) also resolved claims involving the same plaintiffs, with the financial terms of both companies' agreements remaining confidential.

Snap guided for third-quarter revenue of $1.70 billion to $1.74 billion, representing approximately 13% to 15% year-over-year growth.

Analysts expect Snap's annual revenue to reach $8.17 billion by 2028, but declining North American users and potential product restrictions remain important risks.

What Happened?

Snap (SNAP) settled a social media addiction lawsuit on November 2, avoiding a closely watched trial just two days before opening arguments were scheduled to begin in Los Angeles.

Meta Platforms (META) had already resolved claims involving the same two plaintiffs, identified as S.J. and K.D.B. Neither company disclosed the financial terms of its agreements, according to Reuters.

The plaintiffs alleged that engagement features encouraged compulsive social media use among younger users and contributed to mental health problems. Snap disputed the allegations and emphasized safeguards introduced to protect its community.

Although the settlement removes an immediate courtroom risk, the broader legal battle remains unresolved.

Social media companies still face more than 1,600 claims from families and school districts, with additional bellwether trials expected in March 2027.

Lead trial attorney Mark Lanier emphasized the need for "real design changes that protect kids."

That distinction matters for investors because future product restrictions could have longer-lasting financial consequences than an individual settlement payment.

Under a separate agreement with state attorneys general, Meta agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion, according to the New York Attorney General. The agreement remains subject to court approval, and part of the maximum payment depends on other major social media companies adopting similar protections.

Those measures include daily time limits, restrictions on overnight access, and limits on notifications during school hours. Portions of the broader agreement's payments also depend on competing platforms adopting similar protections and making matching payments.

For Snap, the central uncertainty is whether similar requirements could eventually restrict engagement or advertising opportunities.

Can Snap Maintain Revenue Growth Despite Legal Pressure?

Analysts expect Snap's annual revenue to increase from $5.93 billion in 2025 to approximately $8.17 billion by 2028, representing roughly 38% cumulative growth, according to TIKR consensus estimates as of October 31, 2026.

title: What Did Reddit's Quarter Change For Its Stock?
detail:
What Did Reddit's Quarter Change For Its Stock?
Trefis Team
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 3:20 PM EST 3 min read

^GSPC
META
GOOG

Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Reddit (RDDT) stock fell 29.2% on October 30, 2026, during the first trading session after its fiscal Q3 2026 report. The S&P 500 lost 1.8% on the same day. This marks a steep fall following a quarter where revenue of $895 million came in about 2% above what analysts had expected. So what did Reddit tell investors that its results did not?

Reddit Warned Of A Drop In Daily Users

During the October 29 call, management said daily users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter from a current base of 130 million. The warning came from search. Traffic that search engines send to Reddit fell meaningfully in fiscal Q3 2026, and the decline sped up late in the quarter. In October, those referrals dropped by more than 1 million a week on average, and management's estimate for users assumes that pace continues.

The results themselves held no surprise of that size. Earnings per share came in at $1.40, above the $1.33 analysts expected. Reddit's peers fell far less on the same day. Meta Platforms fell 1.5% and Alphabet fell 1.4%, while Pinterest, the weakest of the three peers, fell 2.8%. The fall was Reddit's own, not its industry's.

Is Reddit's Slowdown More Than One Quarter?

It is for sales growth. Reddit's revenue grew 69.1% from a year earlier in fiscal Q1 2026, a shade below the 69.7% posted in fiscal Q4 2025. Growth then slowed to 61.1% in fiscal Q2 2026 and to 53.0% in fiscal Q3 2026. Management expects growth to slow again in fiscal Q4 2026, forecasting revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, or 38% to 42% growth. News reports on October 30 said that outlook was lower than expected. The traffic warning is new, but the slower growth is not.

Profitability is another matter. Reddit reported an operating margin of 29.2% in fiscal Q3 2026, compared with 23.7% a year earlier.

Management argued that Reddit is still growing where it counts: engagement from its app and logged-in users. About 80% of Reddit's monetization happens within that group, management said. The company added that Reddit is still a top search term in Google, and that Google is simply not sending people to Reddit the way it used to.

When Will Reddit's User Count Be Known?

The fiscal Q4 2026 results will be Reddit's first report since the warning. During that quarter, management plans to begin fully testing a logged-in-only version of Reddit in select markets outside the U.S. The company said the change would likely trade reach for engagement, noting that it will keep evaluating how it reports users.

title: Shopify vs. Amazon: Which Stock Wins When AI Agents Do the Shopping?

Shopify vs. Amazon: Which Stock Wins When AI Agents Do the Shopping?

Shopify vs. Amazon: Which Stock Wins When AI Agents Do the Shopping? ©@William_Potter from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Shopify shares fell 8% today after its third-quarter revenue grew 32%, but its merchandise volume came in just short of Wall Street's expectations.

Shopify's checkout runs inside ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Meta's Muse. Amazon is building its own shopping agents and has fought to keep outside ones off its store.

Amazon trades at a much lower multiple of expected earnings, but analysts expect Shopify's earnings to grow faster through 2028: about 33% a year, against about 25% for Amazon.

Shopify looks like the better bet on agentic shopping, as long as the companies that own the agents keep using its checkout at its standard rates.

Shopify (SHOP:NASDAQ) shares fell 8% today after its third-quarter report. The timing is awkward, because Shopify has spent the year pitching itself as the checkout behind every AI shopping agent. Its president, Harley Finkelstein, said in the release that Shopify is "continuing to build commerce into every surface, every agent, and increasingly, everywhere."

Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ), up 11% this year, has a different plan: build its own agents and keep everyone else's off its store.

So if AI assistants end up doing a lot of the buying, which stock wins? Is it the platform behind millions of merchants, or the store that owns the customer?

A strong quarter that missed by a hair

Shopify's third-quarter revenue grew 32% to $3.74 billion, and operating income jumped 66% to $568 million. Free cash flow came to $816 million, a 22% margin and well above the $723 million analysts expected.

But gross merchandise volume (GMV) of $119.1 billion came in just short of the $120.1 billion analysts expected. Shopify had also beaten the top of its own revenue guidance in each of the three quarters before this one. This time, 32% growth landed inside its guide for a low-thirties rate.

For the fourth quarter, Shopify again expects revenue to grow at a low-thirties rate, a touch above the roughly 30% analysts had expected going in.

Not bad at all.

TIKR tracks 54 analysts on Shopify. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Shopify, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Shopify's Analyst Ratings

Shopify plugs into every agent

Shopify merchants already sell through ChatGPT's Instant Checkout. In January, Shopify and Google announced the Universal Commerce Protocol, which runs checkout in Gemini and Google's AI Mode. Microsoft's Copilot has Shopify's checkout built in, and Meta's Muse agent checks out with Shop Pay at Shopify's existing payments rates.
